originality.rationale: Substantive comparison to nearest priors listed in topic.json, not timestamp/failed-search. (a) Henon 1976 + cycle-expansion numerical tables: give period-7 points to double precision at (1.4,0.3) with no rigor, no inclusion proof, no persistence — draft's interval-Newton certificate converts one such point to rigorous existence, delta real. (b) Galias-Zgliczynski computer-assisted chaos / horseshoe (Nonlinearity 11:5): proves topological horseshoe implying infinitely many cycles in some region via covering relations, but names no explicit 1e-09 phase-space box, itinerary-identified period-7 saddle at classical parameters, cone margin, or a-interval — orbit-level named certificate not implied. (c) Benedicks-Carleson / uniformly hyperbolic Henon attractor machinery: proves hyperbolicity at attractor level or away from classical parameters, not a checkable Krawczyk log for this orbit at (1.4,0.3). Internal prior scan (3 Resultary findings: spider mixing, 4-uniform forbidden, J2-free rank; 6 SCOPE failures) has no topical overlap, confirmed disjoint. Web search attempted via webfetch for Henon map and DOI 10.1007/BF01608556 but transport failed (offline environment), so assessment rests on above substantive deltas plus domain knowledge that CAPD-style Krawczyk for Henon orbits is standard but no published box for this P7-A itinerary was identified. Hence the specific interval box+log is new. Method itself is standard interval-Newton, so novelty is instance-level first-certificate, not methodological — sufficient for originality PASS under new-fact sense, with value assessed separately.

value.rationale: Even though correct and new, result is not independently worth finding later: textbook restatement + single enumeration + tiny unmotivated gain. (i) Textbook method: 14-dim Krawczyk/interval-Newton for Henon periodic orbits with trace/det eigenvalue bounds and diagonal-cone Sylvester check is canonical validated-numerics exercise (Tucker/Wilczak/Zgliczynski tutorials; CAPD/INTLAB routinely certify such strongly hyperbolic orbits in minutes). No methodological innovation; huge margins (q 4e-09, cone >900, eigenvalue gaps 34.7/0.99999) show orbit is far from bifurcation and easy. (ii) Mere enumeration: one orbit P7-A among many numerically known Henon cycles, no classification, no fixed symbolic partition (itinerary means cyclic box order only), no counting or optimality. First-box-for-this-itinerary is weak firstness — any tabulated numerical cycle can be boxed routinely. (iii) Tiny unmotivated persistence: d=5e-05 (relative 3.5e-05) with 1e-03 wide tubes, threshold 2.5e-05 arbitrary audit target not tied to any bifurcation or entropy milestone; narrow 1e-09 boxes provably persist only to ~5.48e-10, so advertised narrow boxes are non-robust points, persistence requires 1000x wider tubes. Standard hyperbolic persistence via IFT guarantees some interval; quantifying 5e-05 adds no insight. (iv) Motivated reuse not delivered: draft cites entropy/bifurcation certification and transverse homoclinic forcing positive entropy, but explicitly disclaims any entropy theorem; single saddle without homoclinic/transversality gives no entropy lower bound, no bifurcation-diagram certificate demonstrated, future reuse speculative. Widths/margins are audit criteria, not contributions (draft admits). Therefore falls under reject categories: textbook restatement, mere parameter substitution (classical 1.4,0.3 instance), tiny unmotivated gain, unexplained enumeration even if correct and new.
